title: Product Profile: Cut flowers
subtitle: 2026 Edition
detect_names: Cut flowers and flower buds of a kind suitable for bouquets or for ornamental purposes
Live trees and other plants; bulbs, roots and the like; cut flowers and ornamental foliage
org: Kenya Export Promotion and Branding Agency
intro: Kenya's cut flower industry is the country's best-known horticultural export and one of its largest non-traditional foreign-exchange earners, built on greenhouse production around Lake Naivasha and the central highlands and on a weekly air-freight link to European markets. Roses dominate the export basket, followed by carnations, alstroemeria and a range of summer flowers, and the chain supports estate employment alongside a growing smallholder and out-grower segment.

This profile examines Kenya's trade in cut flowers and flower buds (HS 0603: cut flowers and flower buds of a kind suitable for bouquets or for ornamental purposes, fresh, dried, dyed, bleached, impregnated or otherwise prepared), based on trade values reported to the International Trade Centre (ITC). The analysis covers the period 2021 to 2025.

HS 0603 is reported as a single heading, so the profile is scoped to that heading rather than to a wider product family. The fresh lines that make up the bulk of Kenya's shipments are identified separately in the by-product tables, while the heading total also carries the dried, dyed and otherwise prepared lines.

recommendations: Reduce dependence on the Netherlands and the United Kingdom by building direct volume in the Middle East, Central Asia and North American markets.
Protect the cold-chain and air-freight advantage that makes a two-day farm-to-vase journey possible, since it is the main quality differentiator of Kenyan stems.
Maintain compliance with sustainability, residue and phytosanitary requirements in the destination markets, and expand the range of varieties and summer flowers beyond roses.
